solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Worst place, best time for rest of travellers

parts.note: 'the pits' is slang for the worst place or thing imaginable
top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: A grumble about a dreadful spot that is nonetheless the ideal moment for a weary traveller's break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worst place' and 'best' sit side by side as if contrasting, but each just supplies a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit stop is a short halt on a journey to refuel, eat or stretch the legs.

clue.text: Flier good for advertising

parts.note: a puffin is a seabird, something that flies

explanation.surface: A leaflet that works well for publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a handbill; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To puff is to praise extravagantly in publicity, so puffing is promotional hype.

clue.text: Four or six in test? It's of little significance

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test
IV is four in Roman numerals; VI, six, lands in the same place

explanation.surface: A cricket question about boundaries in a Test match being unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: Either numeral works: TR+IV+IAL and TRI+VI+AL spell the same letters. Four or six suggests boundary hits in a cricket Test.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means unimportant, of little consequence.

clue.text: Workers organised support for driver, a learner

parts.note: TU stands for trade union, workers organised together
a golf tee holds up the ball for a driver

explanation.surface: Union members arranged backing for a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist; it is the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutee is a person taught by a tutor, a student.

clue.text: Put tar on ship for wages

parts.note: to pay a ship's seam is to coat it with tar
a packet is a mail or passenger boat

explanation.surface: An instruction to tar a vessel in return for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A pay packet is the envelope of earnings handed to a worker, so one's salary.

clue.text: Worthless books I penned in hurry

indicators.note: penned in means enclosed, so the books and I go inside the word for hurry

parts.note: rush means hurry
BB is an abbreviation for books (plural of B)

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on books written in a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish used as an adjective, chiefly British, means of poor quality or valueless.

clue.text: As conclusions from earlier case merit further scrutiny, do this?

definitions.text: As conclusions from earlier case merit further scrutiny, do this?

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so take the final letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A legal hint that an earlier case's findings deserve a fresh hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To retry a case is to hold a new trial when earlier findings deserve reexamination.

clue.text: Bad actors ruined e.g. TV show

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A television programme spoilt by its poor cast.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast is a programme transmitted on radio or television.

clue.text: Ring after ring, unusually mounted as exclusive set

indicators.note: after means the round letter comes after the rearranged word
unusually means the letters are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
up means mounted, as in 'up on a horse'

explanation.surface: Rings stacked on display as the mark of an elite clique.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-group is a closed circle of insiders who keep others out, a clique.

clue.text: Person liable to have violent reaction, as opposed to cold feet?

definitions.text: Person liable to have violent reaction
definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone rash and quick-tempered
second meaning: a ... is the opposite of cold feet, top versus bottom and hot versus cold

explanation.walkthrough: Cold feet means nervous reluctance; reversing both words gives the rash, fiery temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead is an impetuous, easily angered person who acts without thinking.

clue.text: Piano isn't commonly carried in carriage

indicators.note: carried in means held within, so the slang word sits inside the carriage

parts.note: a fly is an old one-horse hired carriage
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone apparently remarking that the piano is not usually transported in a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' looks like the instrument, but it is the musical direction meaning softly.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, piano is the direction to play softly, which is to sound quietly.

clue.text: Allowing little time for deliberation

parts.note: though means allowing that, granting that
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A complaint that a schedule leaves hardly any time for careful consideration.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought is careful consideration or reflection on a matter, a synonym of deliberation.

clue.text: Plan for travel, I hear, around popular time

indicators.note: around means the word for hear goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it
in means fashionable or popular
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A traveller describing a schedule built around the busiest season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' reads as hearsay, but I stands alone and hear means try, as a judge does.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerary is a planned route or schedule for a journey.

clue.text: Who, for example, joins a certain slacker in colony?

parts.note: Doctor Who is an example of a doctor, abbreviated DR
one means a certain, as in 'one Mr Smith'

explanation.surface: A quiz-like question about who joins an idle member of some community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Who' looks like a question word; it is the TV time-lord Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male bee that does no work in the hive, so an idler in a bee colony.

clue.text: Dance in a line in party of Americans

indicators.note: in means the letters go inside the party's initials

parts.note: the GOP (Grand Old Party) is the US Republican Party

explanation.surface: A line dance performed at a gathering of Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: A galop is a lively nineteenth-century ballroom dance in duple time.

clue.text: Remarkable events contributing to catastrophe no men anticipated

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Extraordinary happenings that led to a disaster nobody foresaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are striking or extraordinary occurrences, the plural of phenomenon.

clue.text: Something to read as child slept

parts.note: kid means child
napped means slept briefly

explanation.surface: Bedtime reading for a child who dozed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidnapped is Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure novel, a book one could pick up.

clue.text: Run committee that's targeted by pub's competitors

parts.note: to dart is to run quickly
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A committee being run that ends up as the target of the local pub's rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Competitors' suggests rival pubs; it is the darts players in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A dartboard is the circular target at which darts players throw, a fixture of British pubs.

clue.text: Black dog for high-flying rich type

parts.note: jet is a deep glossy black
a setter is a breed of gun dog

explanation.surface: A black dog as the pet of a wealthy socialite.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet-setter is a wealthy person who travels widely for pleasure, literally flying high.

clue.text: President and scholar who, by definition, became famous

definitions.text: scholar who, by definition, became famous
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Samuel ..., the man of letters famed for his Dictionary

explanation.walkthrough: 'By definition' sounds like 'necessarily' but means through his definitions: Samuel Johnson compiled the great 1755 English dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Johnson is the surname of two American presidents and of the eighteenth-century lexicographer Samuel Johnson.

clue.text: Garment that's the last thing painter puts on

definitions.text: the last thing painter puts on
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the final layer of paint applied

explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts on' suggests dressing, which the first meaning plays up; for the painter it is the final layer applied.
explanation.definitionFit: A topcoat is both an overcoat worn outdoors and the finishing layer of paint on a surface.

clue.text: I.e., what to do when coach lacks power?

definitions.text: what to do when coach lacks power?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: ..., haul the broken-down coach away

explanation.walkthrough: Split as TOW IT, the phrase is the advice for a coach (a bus) whose engine has died.
explanation.definitionFit: To wit is a formal phrase meaning namely, exactly what the abbreviation i.e. stands for.

clue.text: Fish is big success in party, in part

indicators.note: in means the success goes inside the party faction

parts.note: a wing is one part of a political party
a hit is a big success

explanation.surface: A fish dish proves the hit of a party, or at least part of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiting is a small sea fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Next occasion for retirement happening in jolly firm

indicators.note: in means the happening word goes inside the firm one

parts.note: tight means very firm; jolly works as the intensifier
on means happening, as in 'the show is on'

explanation.surface: A firm's party where the next retirement is being celebrated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' suggests leaving work, but it means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is the coming evening, the next time one goes to bed.

clue.text: Animal unloaded from ship, possibly

indicators.note: unloaded from says the answer is taken out of the words that follow, like cargo

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A large beast being taken off a vessel, perhaps at a zoo delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus, shortened to hippo, is a large African river mammal.

clue.text: Opposition getting violent about one bill that needs amendment

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: a text that needs amendment must be changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Political resistance turns ugly over a single bill that wants revising.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebellion is armed or violent resistance to authority, which is opposition turned to force.

clue.text: This we can refer to a single top person

definitions.text: This we can refer to a single top person

parts.words: This we can refer to a single top person
parts.note: the 'we' used by a monarch speaking of themself: a plural pronoun for one person at the very top

explanation.walkthrough: The royal we is a monarch using 'we' to mean 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal we is the plural pronoun a sovereign uses to refer to themselves alone.

clue.text: Source of wool a shopping centre turned up

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Wool supplies appearing at a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The llama is a South American animal kept for its fleece.

clue.text: Ostentatious when monarch enters? That's not altogether fair

indicators.note: enters means the monarch goes into the word for ostentatious

parts.note: showy means ostentatious
ER (Elizabeth Regina) stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A grumble that a monarch's flashy entrance is somewhat unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like justice; it is the weather sense, as in fair and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: Showery weather has intermittent rain, so it is only partly fine and dry.

clue.text: Coming to a ruler about unfinished conflict

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: war means conflict
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A sovereign approaching a war that has not yet ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to means regaining consciousness, which is waking up.

clue.text: A couple of things used in many sports, or one in particular

parts.note: the whole phrase names a pair of items; the first of the couple is a net
the second item common to many sports is a ball

explanation.surface: An observation that two pieces of kit appear across sports, and one sport above all.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'A couple of things used in many sports' works as a unit: a net and a ball, which together name the sport that uses both.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team game, popular in Britain and the Commonwealth, where a ball is shot through a netted hoop.

clue.text: Some medicine for man on board

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a dose of liquid medicine
second meaning: a piece in the board game ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor, but it is a playing piece; draughts is the British name for checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: A draught is a single swallowed dose of medicine, and also a checkers piece, called a man.
